musical.title: Frozen
musical.vocal_style: Contemporary Broadway belt with pop influences. Elsa demands a soaring soprano-mezzo belt to a top C. Anna is a warm bright mezzo belt. The score is lush, emotional, and vocally demanding throughout.
musical.synopsis: Elsa has always feared her magical ice powers. On the day of her coronation they are exposed and she flees into the mountains, accidentally plunging Arendelle into eternal winter. Her younger sister Anna sets off to find her with the help of Kristoff, his reindeer Sven, and the loveable snowman Olaf.

roles.name: Elsa
roles.description: The Snow Queen. Isolated, controlled, and carrying an enormous secret. Elsa is one of the great contemporary female leads: a woman whose power is also her wound. She must be regal, vulnerable, and explosive in equal measure.

vocal.style_notes: Requires a powerful contemporary Broadway belt that can sound both icy and deeply emotional. Let It Go demands a full belt to a top C. The voice should feel like power and pain simultaneously.

dance.notes: Elsa's physicality is about controlled power and sudden freedom. The staging of Let It Go is among the most spectacular in contemporary musical theatre.

acting.notes: The arc from frozen isolation to full acceptance of self and love must be completely real.

casting_insights.why: Let It Go is known worldwide. The full role is vocally and dramatically enormous.
casting_insights.common_casting: Powerful soprano-mezzo belts with dramatic presence and vocal stamina.

what_directors_look_for: Let It Go - the belt must be secure and powerful, not reached for
The controlled exterior that contains enormous emotion
The full dramatic range from Act 1 isolation to Act 2 acceptance
Vocal stamina - the show is vocally punishing
tips: Let It Go is the natural audition piece but Monster will distinguish you
Show the restraint before the release - the explosion only means something if the control was real
Work with a vocal coach specialising in contemporary Broadway belt
common_mistakes: Playing Elsa as cold - she is terrified, not cold
Reaching for Let It Go rather than owning it

key_songs.title: Let It Go
key_songs.notes: The defining number. Full belt to top C required.

key_songs.title: Monster
key_songs.notes: Act 2 crisis. Elsa at her most dramatically expansive.

key_songs.title: Show Yourself
key_songs.notes: The Act 2 climax of self-acceptance. Sung with Anna.

roles.name: Anna
roles.description: The irrepressibly warm, occasionally clumsy, completely devoted younger sister. Anna is the emotional engine of the show. Her love for Elsa is the reason everything happens. The show understands that warmth is as powerful as magic.

vocal.style_notes: Warm bright mezzo belt with genuine pop energy. For the First Time in Forever requires both breathless excitement and genuine longing.

dance.notes: Anna's physicality is warm, spontaneous, and slightly clumsy in the most endearing way.

acting.notes: Anna's optimism must never feel naive - she chooses hope the way Elsa chooses control.

casting_insights.why: An equal lead role to Elsa. Anna carries the emotional warmth and drive of the show.
casting_insights.common_casting: Warm belt mezzos with genuine stage charisma and natural comedy instinct.

what_directors_look_for: Genuine warmth and physical aliveness
For the First Time in Forever shows the full range: excitement, longing, hope
Comedy must feel natural - Anna does not know she is funny
Acting depth for the sacrifice scene
tips: For the First Time in Forever is the ideal audition piece
Never play Anna as an ingenue - she is brave and active at every moment
common_mistakes: Playing Anna as sweet rather than warm

key_songs.title: For the First Time in Forever
A Little Thing Called Love
key_songs.notes: The new stage song. Anna's determined warmth in full bloom.

roles.name: Prince Hans
roles.description: The charming prince who is absolutely not what he appears. Hans is the show's great dramatic reveal - perfectly courtly in Act 1, revealed as utterly ruthless in Act 2. Requires an actor who can play genuine warmth so convincingly that the reversal truly shocks.

vocal.style_notes: Clean charming tenor-baritone. Love Is an Open Door should feel completely genuine.

acting.notes: The entire first act must be played with complete sincerity.

casting_insights.why: Requires genuine acting range from complete charm to complete menace.
casting_insights.common_casting: Tenor-baritones with natural stage charm and acting range for a major character reversal.

what_directors_look_for: Love Is an Open Door sung with absolute genuine romantic conviction
Physical assurance of a trained prince
The ability to make the Act 2 reveal believable in retrospect
tips: Show the warmth completely in Act 1
Hans charm must feel real not performed
common_mistakes: Playing Hans with any hint of his true nature in Act 1

key_songs.title: Love Is an Open Door
key_songs.notes: Hans and Anna's whirlwind romance. Must feel completely genuine.

roles.name: Kristoff
roles.description: The gruff reindeer-obsessed ice harvester who saves the day through sheer reliability and genuine goodness. Kristoff is the show's warm heart when Elsa and Anna are in crisis.

vocal.style_notes: Warm rough-edged baritone. Honest, direct, surprisingly tender.

dance.notes: Physical and strong. Comedy is physical rather than verbal.

acting.notes: Kristoff is the show's anchor - reliable decency that makes the fantastical elements feel grounded.

casting_insights.why: A warm strong supporting role with good vocal and comedic requirements.
casting_insights.common_casting: Warm baritones with natural physical comedy and genuine stage warmth.

what_directors_look_for: The gruff exterior that barely conceals genuine warmth
Physical comedy and natural stage presence
Warm baritone quality
tips: Kristoff is not the sharpest person in the room and he knows it
The warmth for Sven and for Anna must be completely genuine
common_mistakes: Playing Kristoff as purely comic - he is also genuinely brave and good

key_songs.title: Reindeer(s) Are Better Than People
key_songs.notes: Kristoff's honest assessment. Warm and funny.

key_songs.title: What Do You Know About Love?

roles.name: Olaf
roles.description: The magical snowman brought to life by Elsa's powers. Innocent, warm, and completely certain that summer will be wonderful. Olaf is the show's pure heart and its finest comic role.

vocal.style_notes: Light warm character tenor with genuine sweetness. In the Right Here should feel like the most sincere thing he has ever said.

dance.notes: Pure comedy - a body made of snow that should not move the way it does. Creative physical performance is central.

acting.notes: Must be genuinely funny without being irritating. The sweetness must be completely genuine for In the Right Here to pay off.

casting_insights.why: Olaf is the show's most beloved character for many audience members.
casting_insights.common_casting: Physical comedians with real acting depth.

what_directors_look_for: Physical comedy that creates a convincing snowman without becoming tiresome
Genuine warmth and innocence must be completely real
In the Right Here: emotion must be fully accessible
tips: Olaf never knows he is funny - always completely sincere
Physical comedy should feel discovered not performed
common_mistakes: Playing Olaf as a small child - he is innocent but not stupid
Making the physical comedy too broad

key_songs.title: In Summer
key_songs.notes: Olaf's famous fantasy about summer. Pure comic joy.

key_songs.title: In the Right Here
key_songs.notes: The new stage song. Heartfelt meditation on love and presence.

roles.name: Duke of Weselton
roles.description: The pompous suspicious opportunistic Duke. The show's comic threat - not the true villain but an effective obstacle. Great character comedy for someone who can dance badly with complete commitment.

vocal.style_notes: Slightly squeaky puffed-up character tenor. Pomposity over talent.

dance.notes: Dances with tremendous confidence and terrible technique. Requires real dance training - dancing badly on purpose is hard.

acting.notes: Complete confidence in his own importance is the whole character.

casting_insights.why: One of the most entertaining character comedy moments in the show.
casting_insights.common_casting: Physical character comedians who can commit to intentional bad dancing.

what_directors_look_for: Comic pomposity
Physical comedy and dancing badly with conviction
The specific threat level - annoying but not dangerous
tips: The bad dancing should look like someone who believes they are dancing beautifully
common_mistakes: Playing the Duke as purely silly - he genuinely believes he is important

key_songs.title: Coronation Sequence
key_songs.notes: The Duke's pompous interjections throughout the coronation.

roles.name: Grand Pabbie
roles.description: The ancient wise troll elder. His prophecies bookend the story and his scenes carry significant dramatic weight despite limited stage time.

vocal.style_notes: Deep warm bass-baritone with genuine authority. Pabbie should sound like someone who has seen centuries.

dance.notes: Distinctive troll physicality. Strong physical character.

acting.notes: Holds the key to everything and must carry genuine mystical authority in brief appearances.

casting_insights.why: A character role with genuine dramatic impact in key scenes.
casting_insights.common_casting: Deep voices with natural authority and character acting depth.

what_directors_look_for: Genuine gravitas
Deep voice with natural authority
Physical distinctness in troll movement
tips: Pabbie's care for both children must be completely real - his warning comes from love
common_mistakes: Playing Pabbie as mysterious rather than wise

key_songs.title: Troll Ensemble
key_songs.notes: Pabbie leads the troll community in welcoming Kristoff and Anna.
